name: Mount Lincoln
generated_description:
Mount Lincoln is a 14,293-foot summit in Colorado. With roughly 3,862 feet of topographic prominence, it stands well above the surrounding terrain. The Mount Lincoln Trail covers 2.4 miles round trip (out-and-back) with about 387 feet of elevation gain — a gradual walk with modest climbing.

The Route

Most of the climbing comes early — the first half of the route does the bulk of the work before the grade eases. The steepest stretch arrives around mile 1.11, gaining roughly 2,500 feet per mile — expect a slow, deliberate pace through here. From the trailhead at about 13,914 feet, the route tops out near 14,232 feet.

Getting There

The trailhead is at 39.33875, -106.1117 (tap for driving directions). It's roughly 65 miles southwest of Denver, Colorado. Arrive early on weekends — trailhead lots at popular peaks fill quickly, and cell service is often unreliable once you leave the highway.

When to Go

The reliable snow-free window is roughly July through September. At this elevation, afternoon thunderstorms are a serious summer hazard — start early and plan to be off the upper mountain by midday. Outside that window expect snow travel and bring traction and navigation skills to match.

Know Before You Go

The Easy rating comes from the National Park Service difficulty formula, which weighs total distance against elevation gain. Most hikers should budget about 1.0 hours of moving time; add margin for breaks, photos and the descent. Download the GPX track from this page before you go — cell coverage is unreliable in the mountains and a saved route works offline in any GPS app. Conditions change: verify current access, closures and weather with the official land manager before you go. Trail data is sourced from OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL).

Looking to link objectives or plan a weekend? Nearby summits include Mount Cameron, Mount Bross and Quandary Peak — each has its own guide on this site.

faqs.answer: The trailhead is at 39.33875, -106.1117 in Colorado. Use the driving-directions link in the Getting There section above, and note that parking at popular trailheads fills early on weekends.

faqs.question: Are dogs allowed on the Mount Lincoln trail?
faqs.answer: Rules vary by land manager — national parks often prohibit dogs on trails, while most national forests allow them on leash. Check with the managing agency for this trail before bringing your dog, and pack out waste.

faqs.question: When is the best time to hike Mount Lincoln?
faqs.answer: July through September is the reliable snow-free window. Start early to avoid afternoon thunderstorms above treeline.

faqs.question: How tall is Mount Lincoln?
faqs.answer: Mount Lincoln stands at 14,293 feet (4,357 meters) in Colorado.
